summary.title: Vim Cheat Sheet & Quick Reference
summary.one_liner: A categorized Vim 8.2 cheat sheet covering motions, editing, operators, text objects, buffers, windows, tabs, search and replace, macros, and marks.
keywords: how to save and quit vim
how to undo redo in vim
how to replace text in vim
how to delete a word in vim
how to split windows in vim
takeaways: Vim motions (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, f/t, gg/G, H/M/L) let you move the cursor quickly without leaving the keyboard.
Operators (d, y, c, >, =) combine with motions and text objects such as iw or i" to edit text precisely.
Search and replace with :%s/old/new/g, including regex and case-conversion flags, plus :g for line-wide actions.
Buffers, windows, and tabs are managed with commands like :e, :bn, <C-w>s, and gt/gT.
Macros are recorded with q{letter} and replayed with @{letter}; the page also lists diff, fold, and marks commands.
summary.summary: This is a quick-reference cheat sheet for Vim 8.2, organized into tables of shortcuts with short descriptions. It covers cursor movement, insert and delete commands, undo and redo, visual mode, operators with counts, text objects, buffers, windows, tabs, search, substitution with regex, global commands, macros, vimdiff, folds, marks, and shell integration. Example commands are shown inline, such as backreference substitutions and clipboard copy commands for macOS and Linux. It is a reference page rather than a step-by-step tutorial.
